findings.description: The reports bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so bucket/object ACLs or policies could grant public access to archived report data.
The bucket has no logging block, so read/write access to potentially sensitive report data is not recorded, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorized access.

Object versioning is not enabled, so objects deleted or overwritten by an attacker (or ransomware) cannot be recovered. Combined with force_destroy = true the bucket contents can be silently destroyed.
The ledger export bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial export data unencrypted at rest with no KMS key control.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so access to ledger exports is not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled on the ledger bucket, so overwritten or deleted financial exports are unrecoverable, and force_destroy = true permits full deletion of contents.
The bucket relies only on a private canned ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a later policy or ACL change could expose ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server-side encryption configuration, so artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket, leaving it exposed to accidental public exposure of model artifacts.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedures and endpoints and would be stored unencrypted.
No logging block is defined, so access to runbook content is not recorded for audit or incident response.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guarding this bucket against public ACLs or bucket policies.
The audit trail bucket itself has no logging block configured, so tampering with or access to the central log destination is not itself logged.
The audit log bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so public ACLs/policies are not blocked on a bucket holding security-relevant logs.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows all audit records to be deleted with a single terraform destroy, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.

The uploaded vendor roster object specifies no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption, and its destination bucket has no default encryption, so this potentially sensitive vendor data is written to S3 in plaintext.
